answer: A threshold BLS beacon produces each random output as a single aggregate signature, and the zenith of the design is that the signature is unique and verifiable against one public key. The island of the protocol is that any quorum of signers can produce the round's randomness, so the beacon never stalls on a few offline members. A Sybil cannot bias the beacon because it would need to control a threshold of signers, and the saffron of the beacon output is the same no matter which quorum signed it.
